A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
                                              Alec Kriebel
                                      ORCID: 0009-0001-9320-500X

                                   Version 1.0 — 12 October 2026


                                                 Abstract
          We apply a negative-mass member of the known Dadhich–Kar–Mukherjee–Visser metric
      family to the regular-zero-area-singularity conjecture in Burtscher’s Oberwolfach report. Its
      natural static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass −2a, but the ho-
      mogeneous weak second Bianchi identity fails under the boundary-reaching vector-test conven-
      tion of Burtscher–Kiessling–Tahvildar-Zadeh. We prove absolute convergence of the full scalar
      contraction for every such compactly supported smooth test and compute its exact boundary
      functional; a normalized radial test gives −8π. The metric and its Einstein tensor are classical,
      and the ﬂux method is already present in the cited weak-identity work. The contribution is this
      explicit counterexample application and its convergence check. The example violates the null
      energy condition. The conclusion concerns the geometric implication in the cited static-foliation
      framework, with no speciﬁed matter model; it asserts neither regularity on every arbitrary tilted
      slice nor an identity for tests smooth after collapsing the boundary sphere to a point.


1    The geometric question and the test convention
Burtscher’s contribution to Oberwolfach Report 40/2021 describes admissible timelike singularities
using regular zero-area singularities (ZAS) of negative mass on spacelike slices, and conjectures
the homogeneous weak Einstein-tensor identity for that class [1, pp. 2232–2233]. The cited tech-
nical framework of Burtscher–Kiessling–Tahvildar-Zadeh (BKTZ) uses static slices and a retained
inner boundary [2, Sections 1.3–1.4]. This note addresses that geometric implication with their
boundary-reaching vector tests. The short report does not give a fully formal deﬁnition for every
nonsymmetric spacetime or explicitly require regularity on every tilted hypersurface. We state
the foliation interpretation explicitly rather than claim to settle every possible strengthening of its
wording. The report’s broader matter and evolution program remains a separate question.
    Fix a > 0 and deﬁne
                                                                                               a
     M = Rt × {x ∈ R3 : |x| ≥ a},          M = int M ,       ρ = |x|,    Sa = {ρ = a},     ϕ=1− .
                                                                                               ρ

The smooth structure of M retains the sphere Sa . Our test space is T = Cc∞ (M ; T M ): smooth
vector-ﬁeld sections with compact support in the manifold-with-boundary topology. Their nor-
mal boundary component need not vanish. This is the convention in BKTZ, Deﬁnition 2.1, the
boundary-support footnote to Theorem 1.1, and the radial term in equation (2.5) [2]. A section of
the tangent bundle at a boundary is not required to be tangent to that boundary.
   We use signature (− + ++), c = GNewton = 1, and Gµν = Ric(g)µν − 21 Rg gµν , with the Ricci
convention
                            Rµν = ∂λ Γλµν − ∂ν Γλµλ + Γλµν Γκλκ − Γκµλ Γλνκ .

For a metric smooth on M , write
                                            ∫

whenever the full scalar contraction is absolutely integrable. On M this equals M Gµν ∇µ ψ ν dVg
pointwise. Lowering a test vector with a singular metric need not preserve boundary smoothness;
independently smooth covectors are not substituted for T . The homogeneous weak identity is
Ig (ψ) = 0 for every test in this speciﬁed class.


2    A classical metric and an explicit counterexample
The metric used below and the aﬃne-lapse family used in its calculation are known. Dadhich–Kar–
Mukherjee–Visser (DKMV) give [3, equations (9)–(15)]
                            (                       )2           (           )4
                               1 − m/(2r̄)                        m
                  ds = − κ + λ
                     2                                       2
                                                         dt + 1 +                 (dr̄2 + r̄2 dΩ2 ),
                               1 + m/(2r̄)                        2r̄

along with its Einstein-tensor components. The substitution
                                                                     ρ+a
                 (m, r̄, κ, λ) = (−2a, ρ, A, B),             Nv =        ,          N = A + BNv            (2)
                                                                     ρ−a

gives gN = −N 2 dt2 + ϕ4 δ, where δ is the Euclidean metric. We take A, B ≥ 0, A + B > 0, so
N > 0. DKMV’s subsequent wormhole parameter classiﬁcation takes m > 0; the negative-mass
substitution here is an application of their metric formula, not an attribution of this later ZAS or
weak-Bianchi conclusion to that classiﬁcation. No new metric family or Einstein tensor is claimed.
The spatial negative-mass Schwarzschild ZAS is also the standard example in Bray–Jauregui [4].

Theorem 1. For a > 0, the metric

                                   g = −ϕ−2 dt2 + ϕ4 (dρ2 + ρ2 dΩ2 )                                       (3)

is static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically ﬂat on M . Every slice of its natural static
foliation is totally geodesic and has a harmonically regular ZAS at Sa of regular mass −2a. Its
inner end is a genuine curvature singularity, timelike in the limiting radial conformal sense. For
every ψ ∈ T , the scalar in (1) is absolutely integrable and
                                        ∫
                                    2                                                     x
                         Ig (ψ) = − 2             ⟨ψspatial , n⟩δ dt dAδ ,          n=      .              (4)
                                   a       R×Sa                                           ρ

In particular there is a test in T with Ig (ψ) = −8π. The eﬀective tensor T = G/(8π) violates the
null energy condition.

    The theorem disproves the proposed implication from regular negative-mass ZAS slice geometry
to the homogeneous identity under the stated foliation and test convention. A speciﬁed matter
system or an added energy condition is not among its hypotheses. We prove the theorem through
the following geometric and analytic calculations; no numerical veriﬁcation is used as a proof of a
quantiﬁed assertion.

2.1   Regular ZAS and the timelike singular end
The resolution (δ, ϕ) extends smoothly to Sa , where ϕ vanishes simply. The Euclidean unit normal
into the exterior is +∂ρ , and
                                             1
                                  ∂ρ ϕ|Sa = > 0,        ∆δ ϕ = 0.
                                             a
These are the regular and harmonic resolution conditions of Bray–Jauregui, Deﬁnitions 6–7 [4].
Their ZAS area condition concerns approaching boundary graphs converging in C 1 (Deﬁnition 4).
For every such family the Euclidean areas stay bounded, while the supremum of ϕ4 on the surfaces
tends to zero. Since dAh = ϕ4 dAδ for h = ϕ4 δ, their physical areas tend to zero. This checks the
full approaching-surface condition, not just coordinate spheres. Deﬁnition 10 then gives

The time-independent spatial metric and zero shift give second fundamental form K = 0. These
statements concern the natural static foliation.

The invariant computed below diverges at this ﬁnite-aﬃne-length end. The timelike statement is
about this limiting causal structure; no nondegenerate smooth extension of the physical four-metric
to the cylinder is asserted.

This is invariant curvature blow-up, despite the zero scalar curvature. In a static orthonormal frame
the energy density is zero and each angular pressure is −a/(8πρ3 ϕ5 ) < 0. An angular null vector
with frame components (1, 0, 1, 0) therefore has T (k, k) < 0, proving the stated NEC violation.


3    Absolute convergence and the exact defect
We establish the full boundary functional for the classical family; its main member gives (4). BKTZ
already use a limiting boundary-ﬂux calculation [2, Deﬁnition 2.1 and the calculation following
equation (2.5)]. Here the necessary convergence is proved directly, without invoking their suﬃcient
theorem outside its hypotheses.
Proposition 1. For a > 0, A, B ≥ 0, A + B > 0, let gN be deﬁned by (2). For every ψ ∈ T the
full contraction is absolutely integrable and
                                                     ∫
                                                4A
                                  IgN (ψ) = −                  ⟨ψspatial , n⟩δ dt dAδ .                    (10)
                                                a2    R×Sa

Thus the homogeneous identity for every test in T holds within this family exactly when A = 0.
Proof. In exterior Cartesian coordinates dVgN = N ϕ6 dt d3 x. Equation (7) and r3 = ρ3 ϕ6 give the
weighted mixed spatial tensor
                                                           Aa
                                    Di j := N ϕ6 Gi j =       (6ni nj − 2δij ).                            (11)
                                                           ρ3
It is Euclidean symmetric, traceless, and smooth up to ρ = a > 0. Writing ϕi = ∂i ϕ, the spatial
connection is
                  2 j                                               2(                             )
         Γjik =    (δ ϕk + δkj ϕi − δik ϕj ),        Di j Γjik =       (tr D)ϕk + Di k ϕi − Dk j ϕj = 0.
                  ϕ i                                               ϕ

                                                           4
The time row and column of Gµ ν vanish, and Γjit = 0. Hence, pointwise on M ,

                                         Gµ ν ∇µ ψ ν dVgN = Di j ∂i ψ j dt d3 x.                (12)

On the compact support of any ψ ∈ T , D and the Cartesian ﬁrst derivatives of ψ are bounded,
including at the boundary. The support has ﬁnite Euclidean measure. Thus the absolute value of
the right side is integrable. This proves convergence for arbitrary time and angular dependence
and avoids spherical-coordinate pole issues.
    The radial and tangential eigenvalues of D are Dr = 4Aa/ρ3 and DT = −2Aa/ρ3 . Consequently
                                                (                        )
                                                    2
                                     ∂i Di j = Dr′ + (Dr − DT ) nj = 0.
                                                    ρ

Integrate (12) by parts over a+ε < ρ < R, with R and the time endpoints outside the support. The
inner outward Euclidean normal of this exterior domain is −n. The only boundary contribution is
                                                    ∫
                                           4Aa
                                     −                       ⟨ψspatial , n⟩δ dt dAδ .
                                         (a + ε)3   R×Sa+ε

Absolute convergence of the interior integral and smoothness of the boundary trace permit ε ↓ 0,
proving (10). At A = 0 the Einstein tensor is identically zero. For A > 0 the radial test below has
nonzero functional, proving the ﬁnal assertion.
                                 ∫
    Choose η ∈ Cc∞ (R) with          η dt = 1 and χ ∈ Cc∞ ([a, ∞)) equal to 1 near a. Set

                                                    ψ = η(t)χ(ρ)∂ρ .                            (13)

Since ∂ρ = xi ∂xi /ρ and a > 0, this is smooth on M and has a nonzero normal boundary trace.
Its spherical components are angular independent, meeting also the convenient restriction used in
BKTZ’s equation (2.5). Formula (10) gives IgN (ψ) = −16πA, hence −8π at A = B = 1/2. As a
direct sign and density check, its complete scalar density is
                             (                      )
                                 χ′ (ρ) χ(ρ)
                   4Aaη(t)             − 2              dt dρ dΩ = 4Aaη(t)∂ρ (χ/ρ) dt dρ dΩ.
                                   ρ     ρ

The boundary endpoint is χ(a)/a = 1/a, which gives the same negative sign. This completes the
proof of Theorem 1.
    Individual connection summands in this radial computation can each have logarithmically diver-
gent integrals. Equation (12) combines the ordinary smooth summands on M before integration. It
does not separately integrate divergent terms, take a principal value, multiply tensor distributions,
or assign a nonsingular boundary value to the physical metric.


4    Scope, checks, and disclosure
The counterexample has nonzero order (ρ − a)−5 mixed Einstein components. In particular, with
x = ρ − a, x5 Gρ ρ → 2a3 ̸= 0. BKTZ Theorem 1.1 assumes the strictly improved bound O(x−5+κ )
for some κ > 0 [2]; it does not cover this borderline case. The old boundary-ﬂux method and
the independent convergence proof are distinct from an invocation of that suﬃcient theorem. The
vacuum control A = 0, B > 0 is the negative-mass Schwarzschild vacuum spacetime after time
rescaling and has zero functional. Sharing its spatial metric does not make the main lapse vacuum.


                                                             5
    The static-slice condition is essential to the claim’s formulation. Bray–Jauregui use a time-
symmetric setting and discuss extensions beyond it separately [4, p. 3 and Section 6.6 of the arXiv
version]. For example, a uniformly spacelike local tilt t = t0 + qs(ρ), |q| < 1, has induced metric
                             (                      )                          2a
                     hq = ϕ4 (1 − q 2 )dρ2 + ρ2 dΩ2 ,       mreg (hq ) = −          < 0.
                                                                             1 − q2
Its resolution remains √
                       smooth and positive. Arbitrary nearly null tilts need not have that property:
t = u(ρ) with u′ = ϕ3 1 − ϕ2 is interior-spacelike but has induced metric ϕ6 dρ2 + ϕ4 ρ2 dΩ2 . Any
simple deﬁning conformal factor in the retained cylinder structure leaves a zero radial eigenvalue
in the resolved boundary metric. No all-arbitrary-tilted-slices assertion is made.
    Tests conﬁned to the open interior give the ordinary classical identity, and tests smooth after
collapsing Sa to a point have a diﬀerent smoothness requirement. In particular the radial test (13)
must not be replaced through that collapse. The eﬀective matter violates NEC, so neither an energy-
constrained version nor a speciﬁed electromagnetic matter system is resolved. The conclusion is
the failure of the geometric implication in the stated boundary/static framework.
    The accompanying archive preserves the thirteen available historical sources and supplies ex-
plicitly guarded normal/optimized reproductions and independent exact consistency checks. Its
provenance note distinguishes eleven veriﬁed payload references from one unavailable, unattested
standalone manifest digest. The analytic proof establishes the quantiﬁed conclusion; ﬁnite compu-
tations provide supporting falsiﬁcation evidence, not proof by sampling.
    A bounded independent literature search found no earlier printed application of this metric
resolving the exact report conjecture in the inspected routes. This is not a certiﬁcate of historical
ﬁrst priority or continued openness. The metric, tensor, spatial ZAS example and boundary-ﬂux
method are attributed to the sources above. The supporting priority ledger records search coverage
and its limits.

AI use and review status. AI tools were used extensively in developing, writing, reproducing
and adversarially checking this work, including parallel AI reviews. This is an unrefereed research
note. No independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant veriﬁcation is claimed.
